summary: Laurie L. Patton works in Indology and religious studies. She studied at Choate Rosemary Hall, Harvard, and the University of Chicago. She held posts at Emory University (~1996–2011), Duke University (~2011–2015), and Middlebury College (~2015–2024).

Lawrence E. Sullivan is a scholar of religious studies. He served as Director at Harvard University from circa 1990 to 2003 and as Professor of Theology at the University of Notre Dame from circa 2004 to 2014.

Lawrence McCrea is an Indologist, philosopher, and linguist. He studied at Cornell University and the University of Chicago under Sheldon Pollock from circa 1991 to 1998, later taking a post at Cornell University in circa 2008.

Lawrence William Nelson is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Butler, Indiana, New York, and Northwestern Universities, the College of Santa Fe, St. John's College, and earned a doctorate from the California Institute of Integral Studies.

Le Manh That works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned a BA at the University of Saigon and a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison before serving at Van Hanh University from 1974 to 1975.

LeRoy Carr Barret was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Washington and Lee University from circa 1895 to 1898 and under Maurice Bloomfield at Johns Hopkins University from circa 1899 to 1903.

Leah Judith Zahler studied Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She received her PhD from the University of Virginia around 1994 under Jeffrey Hopkins, having also studied under Karen C. Lang, Paul Groner, Julian Hartt, Harvey B. Aronson, and Geshe Wangyal.

Leedom Lefferts specializes in religious studies and anthropology. He served at Drew University as Professor Emeritus of Anthropology starting around 1972 and held a post as a Research Associate in Anthropology at the Smithsonian Institution.

Leela Aditi Wood works in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. She completed her PhD at the University of Michigan under Luis Oscar Gómez and Martin J. Powers, and held a post at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute.
Lennert Gesterkamp is a scholar in sinology and religious studies. He studied at SOAS University of London and completed his studies at Leiden University under Kristofer Schipper and Eugene Y. Wang.

Leo M. Pruden specialized in Buddhist studies. He studied under Taitetsu Unno and with Akira Hirakawa at the University of Tokyo, later holding posts at Brown University, the Nyingma Institute, and the University of Oriental Studies.

Leo Meyer was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at the University of Göttingen and Humboldt University of Berlin under Theodor Benfey, Franz Bopp, and Moriz Haupt. He held posts at Göttingen and the Imperial University of Dorpat.

Leo Weisgerber was a linguist. He held academic posts at the University of Rostock (~1925–1927), Pedagogic Academy Bonn (~1927–1930), the University of Marburg (~1930–1938), and the University of Bonn (~1942–1967).

Leon Hurvitz worked in Buddhist studies, sinology, and Japanology. He held professorial posts at the University of Washington in 1965 and at the University of British Columbia from circa 1971 to 1988.

Leonard Bloomfield was a linguist who studied at Harvard, Wisconsin, Chicago, Leipzig, and Göttingen. He held posts at Cincinnati, the University of Illinois System, Ohio State, the University of Chicago, and Yale University.
Leonard C. D. C. Priestley works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and sinology. He studied under Anthony Kennedy Warder and F. E. L. Priestley, and held a post at the University of Toronto.

Leonard van der Kuijp is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He held an assistant professorship at the University of Washington from circa 1987 to 1994 and became Department Chair at Harvard University in 1995.

Indologist Leopold von Schroeder studied at Tartu, Jena, Leipzig, and Tübingen under Leo Meyer and Rudolf von Roth. He held posts at the University of Tartu, University of Innsbruck, University of Vienna, and the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

Leslie S. Kawamura was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Saskatchewan under Herbert V. Guenther and later served as Professor at the University of Calgary.

Levi McLaughlin works in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo and Princeton, and held posts at Kokugakuin University, Wofford College, National University of Singapore, University of Iowa, and North Carolina State University.
